summary: Repository data exist for otolith and bivalve increments with dates or environmental context (PANGAEA Sprattus otolith microstructure series, Glycymeris and Arctica islandica increments; Dryad cod annual increments, 5.3 MB CSV; NOAA rockfish otolith growth linked to upwelling). Nothing was found for starch grains or bones, and I did not confirm that any one record pairs increments with an independent seasonal or diel marker per specimen.
next_step: Open PANGAEA 982536 and 816206 and the Dryad cod CSV header to see which have an independent time axis; pre-register on bivalve/otolith series only and state that scales, bones and starch grains are untested.
obstacles_confirmed: Starch grains and most bones are poorly represented next to commercial fish otoliths and bivalve bands.
Environmental covariates and internal rhythms can be correlated, so records with only an environmental series do not separate the two.
